sentences.text: Technosaurus is an extinct genus of silesaurid dinosauriforms named after Texas Tech University.
It belongs to the infraclass Archosauromorpha, the unranked order Ornithodira, and the parent group Sulcimentisauria.
Sankar Chatterjee named the genus and its type species T. smalli in 1984.
The original description relied on specimen TTUP P9021, which included a premaxilla, two lower jaw pieces, a vertebra, and an astragalus.
The genus is placed within the family Silesauridae, although the Paleobi Database classifies it in the class Ornithischia.
However, the Paleobi Database classifies Technosaurus in the class Ornithischia, which differs from the placement in the family Silesauridae.
This animal lived during the Late Triassic, specifically the Norian stage, between 227.3 and 205.7 million years ago.
Fossils were found in the Cooper Canyon Formation and the Bull Canyon Formation, both part of the Dockum Group in Texas, United States.
Irmis et al. (2007) found no unambiguously dinosaurian characteristics in the skull fragments of Technosaurus.
Later studies concluded that Technosaurus is a valid genus but cannot be definitively classified beyond Archosauriformes incertae sedis.
